nodes.text: Focus on the visitor who purchased the maximum number of tickets.

To find the details of the visitor who purchased the maximum number of tickets, we can use the following SQL query: SELECT v.visitor_id, v.name, v.email, v.address, v.phone, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS total_tickets_purchased FROM visitors v JOIN tickets t ON v.visitor_id = t.visitor_id GROUP BY v.visitor_id ORDER BY total_tickets_purchased DESC LIMIT 1.
The query retrieves relevant visitor details like visitor_id, name, email, address, phone, and the total_tickets_purchased count.
Retrieve the visitor's name as part of the details.
To retrieve the visitor's name as part of the details, we can modify the SQL query to include v.name.

The modified query is: SELECT v.visitor_id, v.name, v.email, v.address, v.phone, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS total_tickets_purchased FROM visitors v JOIN tickets t ON v.visitor_id = t.visitor_id GROUP BY v.visitor_id ORDER BY total_tickets_purchased DESC LIMIT 1.
Ensure the ticket purchase was all in a single transaction.
To ensure that the maximum number of tickets purchased was done in a single transaction, we can modify the SQL query by joining the transactions table.

The updated query is: SELECT v.visitor_id, v.name, v.email, v.address, v.phone, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS total_tickets_purchased FROM visitors v JOIN tickets t ON v.visitor_id = t.visitor_id JOIN transactions tr ON t.transaction_id = tr.transaction_id GROUP BY v.visitor_id ORDER BY total_tickets_purchased DESC LIMIT 1.
Retrieve the visitor's age along with the name.
To retrieve the visitor's age along with their name, we can modify the SQL query by including TIMESTAMPDIFF().

The updated query will be: SELECT v.visitor_id, v.name, TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, v.date_of_birth, CURDATE()) AS age, v.email, v.address, v.phone, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS total_tickets_purchased FROM visitors v JOIN tickets t ON v.visitor_id = t.visitor_id JOIN transactions tr ON t.transaction_id = tr.transaction_id GROUP BY v.visitor_id ORDER BY total_tickets_purchased DESC LIMIT 1.
